Source: A 51-year-old man presents to the emergency department complaining of fever and a cough with yellow-green sputum for the past 3 days.
He was diagnosed with lobar pneumonia and completed a 7-day course of antibiotics with complete resolution of his symptoms.
He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes a day for 35 years and drinks 3 beers per week.
He has no other significant medical history and does not take any medications.
He is sexually active with his wife.
A chest radiograph is ordered and reveals a consolidation in the right middle lobe.
Chest radiograph performed at the time was notable for a right middle lobe consolidation.
He denies any hemoptysis, facial pain, rhinorrhea, or night sweats.
Physical exam is notable for decreased breath sounds on the right side without wheezing and increased dullness to percussion on the right side.
